Works from the `Brief` of `idea-repo` (wiki revision 3; its page header still reads "revision 2"). ## 1. The story in one paragraph

Pairwise-comparison leaderboards (Chatbot Arena, MT-Bench, sports ratings) are Bradley–Terry fits whose published uncertainty is a bootstrap CI. A CI answers "would another sample of the same process reorder the models?". It does not answer the two questions readers and attackers actually have: *how many of the existing comparisons carry this conclusion*, and *is that number large or small for a dataset of this size and spread?* The raw answer ("dropping 0.1% of the votes flips the top model") is expected not to be comparable across datasets, because theory says the number of alterations needed grows with the statistical separation z and with √N; whether this holds on real data is tested in 5.1 and first on synthetic BT data, and the introduction's example is written to match whichever way it comes out. We give a common scale (alterations in standard-error units, compared against a parametric-bootstrap null of the same graph) and apply it to crowd, expert, LLM-judge and sports data, with matched contrasts that separate "design" from "statistics".
